Title: Upward convergence: digital regulations and digital firms’ internationalization
Authors: Chang Liu, Pengxiang Zhang, Stephanie Lu Wang
Abstract: Abstract Digital regulations are often portrayed as barriers to digital firms’ internationalization because they hinder digital firms’ market penetration and fragment their global operations. We argue, however, that regulations may play a different role for digital firms that internationalize through virtual presence. Leveraging the European Union’s (EU’s) General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) as context, we examine how the GDPR affects digital products’ penetration in the EU and whether it drives operational fragmentation between EU and non-EU markets. We theorize that the GDPR does not uniformly reduce penetration opportunities; instead, it benefits low data-dependent products and explorative products that differ substantially from firms’ prior offerings. Moreover, building on digital firms’ reliance on network effects, we propose that digital firms may treat the EU as a global benchmark and release EU-penetrated products to non-EU markets, converging upward rather than separating their international operations, thus strengthening the positive association between EU penetration and subsequent non-EU entry. We found support for our hypotheses by analyzing international user-acquisition activities of the top 500 mobile game developers. Our findings contribute to international business research by showing that digital regulations can create new penetration opportunities and act as institutional catalysts that standardize digital firms’ cross-border expansion.

Title: Moving beyond entry modes: toward a new paradigm of international involvement in an era of digitalization and global transitions
Authors: Noman Shaheer, Sali Li, Liang Chen, Keith D. Brouthers, Dan Li, Peter Liesch
Abstract: 我们试图通过将焦点从静态的单一进入模式选择转向动态的多种参与模式组合，重新概念化国际化战略。在一个由人工智能、区块链和机器人技术推动的快速技术变革的、由贸易战和暴力冲突引发地缘政治动荡的、以及日益增长的可持续性需求的时代，跨国公司（MNC）需要重新思考如何应对多样化的利益相关者期望，优先考虑灵活性和可逆性，并在追求效率的同时融入共同创造与合法性。在扩展Brouthers等人（2022）研究的基础上，我们将交易成本经济学与资源基础观点、制度理论、机会视角及生态系统视角相结合，以解释MNC如何随时间配置和重构各种国际参与模式的组合，从而应对快速变化的利益相关者期望。我们进一步综合了本期关于国际参与的专题论文，为理解复杂的、非线性的国际化轨迹提供了实证和理论洞见，并将国际参与框定为一个适应性强、相互关联的系统，以更好地适应当今多目标的全球商业环境。 International business research is at a turning point due to rapid technological changes, geopolitical shifts, and sustainability demands. Traditional theories that focus on single-entry modes, like exporting or joint ventures, are becoming outdated. These theories often view entering foreign markets as a one-time decision aimed at reducing costs. However, multinational corporations (MNCs) now face complex environments that require them to engage with international markets in more dynamic and flexible ways. This article highlights the need for a new approach that considers a broader range of international involvement activities, including digital and non-traditional forms, to better capture the realities of global business today. This article explores how MNCs can adapt to these changes by using a concept called "international involvement constellations." This approach goes beyond traditional entry modes to include various ways MNCs can engage with foreign markets, such as digital platforms and partnerships. The article uses case studies and theoretical insights to show how MNCs can configure and reconfigure their involvement across different markets. This involves combining multiple modes of involvement, like digital engagement and local partnerships, to meet the diverse and changing demands of stakeholders, including customers, governments, and communities. The article emphasizes the importance of flexibility, adaptability, and stakeholder engagement in these constellations. The findings suggest that MNCs need to move away from focusing solely on cost efficiency and control. Instead, they should consider how to balance different involvement modes to create value for various stakeholders. This involves understanding how different modes interact and support each other across markets. The article concludes that this new approach can help MNCs better navigate the complexities of the global business environment. It also calls for future research to explore how these constellations can be managed and evolved over time, considering factors like digital transformation, geopolitical risks, and sustainability goals. This shift in perspective offers a more comprehensive understanding of international business and provides a framework for MNCs to thrive in an increasingly interconnected and uncertain world. Title: What makes an internationalizing firm entrepreneurial?
Authors: Daniel R. Clark, Robert J. Pidduck, Nicole E. Coviello
Abstract: Abstract Zahra et al. (2024) argue that prior research has insufficient understanding of the entrepreneurial nature of internationalization. To address this, they integrate theories from management and international business to develop a firm-level typology that incorporates (1) the degree of radicalness of the firm’s entrepreneurial behavior and (2) the firm’s level of foreign market commitment. We advance these efforts by proposing that, to understand what makes an internationalizing firm entrepreneurial, researchers will also benefit from direct insights from entrepreneurship research. We retain Zahra et al.’s (2024) behavioral focus in our arguments but shift attention to the individuals that guide the firm’s pursuit of international opportunity, regardless of whether the firm is a new venture or an MNE. We also argue that, when compared to typologies, a process-based perspective is better suited to both differentiating firms and to understanding and explaining the dynamic nature of entrepreneurial internationalization behavior and outcomes.

Title: How (much) does country matter to CSR? A variance decomposition study
Authors: Steve Sauerwald, David J. Skandera, Tang Wang
Abstract: 国家层面的影响对于企业社会责任 (CSR) 绩效至关重要。尽管先前的研究揭示了哪些国家层面的变量能够预测企业CSR绩效, 我们对CSR绩效的方差中有多少是由国家层面的系统性影响所解释的知之甚少。我们进行了一项溯因方差分解研究, 以估算CSR方差中由国家层面解释的比例, 并将其与企业、行业和地区层面的影响进行比较, 同时探讨集体主义文化环境如何改变国家层面影响的相对重要性。研究基于2003年至2022年间59个国家的2324家企业共21,766个观察值的面板数据分析显示, 国家效应可以解释企业之间约10%的CSR绩效差异, 超过了行业和区域效应的解释力。在低制度性集体主义和高内群体集体主义的文化环境中, 国家效应更强。 Les influences au niveau du pays jouent un rôle important pour la performance en matière de RSE. Bien que des recherches antérieures aient identifié des variables spécifiques au niveau du pays qui prédisent la performance en RSE des entreprises, nous savons peu de choses sur la part de la variance de la performance en RSE qui peut être expliquée par des influences systématiques au niveau du pays. Nous menons une recherche abductive de décomposition de la variance afin d'estimer la proportion de la variance de la RSE expliquée au niveau du pays, par rapport aux niveaux de l'entreprise, de l'industrie et de la région, ainsi que la manière dont les environnements culturels, sous la forme du collectivisme, modifient l'importance relative des influences au niveau du pays. Une analyse d’un panel de données couvrant 21766 observations provenant de 2324 entreprises réparties dans 59 pays sur la période 2003-2022 révèle que les effets liés au pays expliquent environ 10 % de la variation de la performance en RSE entre les entreprises, dépassant ainsi le pouvoir explicatif des effets liés à l'industrie et à la région. Les effets liés au pays sont plus marqués dans les environnements culturels caractérisés par un faible collectivisme institutionnel et un collectivisme intra-groupe élevé This article explores how country-level factors influence the corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance of multinational enterprises. While previous research has focused on individual country-level factors, this study aims to understand the combined impact of these factors on CSR performance. This article uses data from 21,766 observations of 2324 firms across 59 countries from 2003 to 2022. The data were collected from LSEG’s ESG database, which provides detailed information on firms’ CSR efforts, and cultural data were obtained from the GLOBE project. The researchers employed a variance decomposition approach to determine how much of the CSR performance variance is explained at different levels, such as firm, industry, region, and country. The study also considers the role of collectivism, a cultural trait that emphasizes group cohesion and collective interests, in moderating the impact of country-level influences on CSR performance. The results indicate that country-level factors explain about 10% of CSR performance variance, more than industry or regional factors. In countries with high institutional collectivism, country-level factors explain only about 3% of the variance, while in countries with high in-group collectivism, they explain over 13%. This suggests that cultural factors like collectivism can either amplify or diminish the impact of country-level influences on CSR performance. The study concludes that understanding the cultural context is crucial for multinational enterprises when deciding whether to standardize or localize their CSR strategies. The findings highlight the importance of considering country-level and cultural factors in international CSR research. Title: Foreignness-based social comparison and strategic change: which peer groups matter and when?
Authors: Pengcheng Ma, Lin Cui, Wenping Ye, Stephen X. Zhang
Abstract: Avanzamos en la aplicación de la teoría conductual de la empresa (BTOF, por sus siglas en inglés) en el contexto internacional al desarrollar y validar un marco de comparación social basado en la condición de extranjero. Más allá de la comparación social basada en la industria, nuestro novedoso marco destaca lacondición de extranjero como una base para que las empresas extranjeras identifiquen grupos de referencia social durante sus operaciones internacionales. Argumentamos que la condición de extranjeroes un constructo social de múltiples capas, que incluye una capa indiferenciada compartida por todas las empresas extranjeras en los países receptores, y una capa diferenciada asociada con sus países de origen. Teorizamos que las empresas extranjeras comparan su desempeño simultáneamente con dos grupos de referencia (es decir, pares extranjeros y pares del país de origen) para realizar un diagnóstico de desempeño que conduce a cambios estratégicos. Además, las condiciones institucionales del paísanfitrión moderan estos efectos de comparación social al redirigir la asignación de atención de las empresas extranjeras entre los dos grupos. Cuando estas condiciones alteran las desventajas y beneficios asociados con la condición de extranjero, la prominencia de la condición de extranjero indiferenciada cambia en relación con la condición de extranjero diferenciada, lo que resulta en un desplazamiento de la atención gerencial entre la comparación social basada en pares extranjeros y la basada en pares del país de origen. A través de un análisis de los cambios estratégicos en un panel de empresas extranjeras que operan en China, nuestros hallazgos empíricos respaldan el marco de comparación social basado en lacondición de extranjero al esclarecer los efectos simultáneos de las comparaciones sociales duales y losdesplazamientos de atención entre ellas. 我们通过开发和验证一个基于外来性的社会比较框架, 推进了企业行为理论 (BTOF) 在国际情境中的应用。超越基于行业的社会比较, 我们的新框架突出了外来者身份作为外国企业在国际运营中识别社会参照群体的基础。我们认为, 外来者身份是一个多层次的社会建构, 包括东道国中所有外国企业共有的无差异化层面, 以及与其来自于同一母国的外国企业相关的差异化层面。我们从理论上阐述了外国企业会同时以两个参照群体 (即外国同行和母国同行) 为基准进行绩效诊断, 从而带来战略变革。此外, 东道国的制度条件通过改变外国企业在这两个群体之间的注意力分配, 调节了这些社会比较的效果。当这些条件改变了与外来者身份相关的劣势和优势时, 无差异化外来者身份的显著性相对于差异化外来者身份发生变化, 从而导致管理者在基于外国同行和基于本国同行的社会比较之间的注意力转移。通过对在华运营的外国企业面板数据进行战略变革分析, 我们的实证研究结果支持了基于外来性的社会比较框架, 阐明了双重社会比较的同时效应以及它们之间的注意力转移机制。 Nous faisons progresser l'application de la théorie comportementale de l'entreprise (the Behavioral Theory of the Firm - BTOF) dans un contexte international en développant et en validant un cadre théorique de comparaison sociale basée sur l’extranéité. Allant au-delà de la comparaison sociale basée sur l'industrie, notre cadre théorique novateur met en évidence l'extranéité comme base pour l'identification des groupes de référence sociale par les entreprises étrangères lors de leurs opérations internationales. Nous argumentons que l'extranéité est une construction sociale à plusieurs niveaux, comprenant une couche indifférenciée partagée par toutes les entreprises étrangères dans les pays hôtes et une couche différenciée associée à leurs pays d'origine. Nous théorisons que les entreprises étrangères comparent simultanément deux groupes de référence (à savoir leurs pairs étrangers et leurs pairs du pays d'origine) pour établir un diagnostic de performance qui conduit à des changements stratégiques. De plus, les conditions institutionnelles du pays hôte modèrent ces effets de comparaison sociale en réorientant l'allocation d’attention des entreprises étrangères entre les deux groupes. Lorsque ces conditions modifient les handicaps et les avantages associés à l’extranéité, la prééminence de l’extranéité indifférenciée change par rapport à celle de l’extranéité différenciée, entraînant un déplacement de l'attention managériale entre la comparaison sociale basée sur les pairs étrangers et celle basée sur les pairs du pays d'origine. Title: Financial statement comparability and employment stability around the world
Authors: Inder K. Khurana, Rong Irene Zhong
Abstract: Abstract In a global economy prone to demand shocks, firms increasingly rely on implicit contracts to stabilize employment. We investigate whether financial statement comparability strengthens these contracts by enabling employees to benchmark their firm’s performance against that of peers, facilitating mutual risk sharing. Using firm-level data from 44 countries, we find that higher comparability reduces layoffs during downturns and tempers aggressive hiring during upturns, consistent with balanced labor adjustment under implicit contracting. Employees at high-comparability firms are also more willing to accept lower wages without compromising productivity, reflecting enhanced trust and cooperation. Further analyses suggest that comparability improves employees’ ability to monitor firm behavior, particularly when social safety nets are strong, earnings are transparent, industries are competitive, and firms deviate from peer norms. Exploiting the mandatory adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as an exogenous shock to comparability supports causal inference. Overall, our findings highlight comparability as a powerful governance mechanism that aligns firm–employee incentives in implicit employment contracts and offers practical guidance for managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen labor market resilience across diverse institutional contexts.

Title: Do political systems affect economic outcomes? The geography of inward FDI and its relationships with growth and inequality
Authors: Dario Maimone Ansaldo Patti, Ram Mudambi, Pietro Navarra
Abstract: Abstract This paper explores the complex interplay between political systems, foreign direct investment (FDI), and income inequality. Building on Acemoglu and Robinson’s Nobel Prize-winning work on institutions, we develop a framework to analyze governments’ political incentives to attract FDI. We argue that highly entrenched autocracies, facing little internal competition for rents, and democracies with strong political competition, eager to secure growth for electoral advantage, exhibit strong incentives to attract FDI. In contrast, weaker autocracies with internal competition for rents and entrenched democracies, where rulers face less pressure to deliver growth, have lower incentives to do so. Rising inequality introduces an additional layer of complexity: while democracies may encounter public resistance to FDI when its benefits are perceived as unevenly distributed, autocracies remain less constrained by public opinion. We analyze data from 144 countries spanning 1990–2018, assessing how political incentives shape FDI inflows and their subsequent impact on economic growth. Our findings suggest that in democracies, robust political competition underpins a country’s incentive to remain attractive to investors, while autocracies require regulatory stability and credible long-term commitments to achieve this outcome. Ultimately, our research underscores a paradox—democratic freedoms, though vital, may at times hinder economic competitiveness relative to autocratic regimes.

Title: In a ‘bad’ place? Location and the relationship between tax haven use and corporate reputation
Authors: Giulio Nardella, Chris Jones, Stephen Brammer, Yama Temouri
Abstract: While tax haven use by multinational enterprises (MNEs) has been associated with significant societal harm, studies have theorized a limited relationship between tax haven use and corporate reputation. This is surprising, given the wealth of evidence illustrating how corporate reputations are frequently undermined by socially harmful activity. To advance our understanding, this study investigates the underexplored heterogeneity associated with tax havens—specifically their location characteristics. Drawing on attribution theory and the country reputation perspective, we theorize and explain how MNE presence in tax havens—of different sizes and country-specific reputations—shapes stakeholder perception, thereby differentially undermining corporate reputations. The results of our longitudinal (2010–2023), firm fixed-effects analysis, involving 559 MNEs, illustrate how MNE engagement with small tax haven economies, as well as locations with adverse country reputations, undermines corporate reputations. Moreover, we demonstrate how MNE engagement with corrupt nation-states can, at times, strengthen the reputational implications of tax haven use. Overall, our research highlights how the risks associated with tax haven use may be greater for some tax haven locations than others. Among our principal contributions, this study advances our understanding of the relationship between tax haven use and corporate reputation.

Title: Correction: Techno-nationalism’s paradox in international standard setting
Techno-nationalism’s paradox in international standard setting
Abstract: Abstract Grounded in realism, geopolitical techno-nationalism advocates restricting technology outflows to targeted entities from rival countries to safeguard national security and technological superiority. We examine this logic in international standard-setting organizations (ISSOs), which exemplify decentralized innovation ecosystems that shape future-generation technologies. We identify a paradox: techno-nationalist restrictions would unintentionally undermine, rather than strengthen home-country firms’ influence over international standards relative to targeted foreign firms. This paradox emerges because techno-nationalist logic clashes with two defining features of decentralized innovation ecosystems: (1) multilateral complementarity, where complementary knowledge needed to co-create value is widely distributed among firms, and (2) emergent technological evolution, where multiple potential trajectories exist and the eventual technological path is socially constructed. Both features make interaction and coordination between firms in ISSOs essential for influencing standards, yet technology disclosure restrictions directly disrupt these processes. The backfiring effect intensifies when home firms exhibit deep technological complementarity with targeted foreign companies, engage in early-stage standardization, or pioneer frontier innovations requiring ecosystem-wide validation. Evidence from the recent U.S. sanctions on Huawei in an influential ISSO supports our hypotheses. Our findings caution policymakers that techno-nationalist controls may backfire in decentralized innovation ecosystems and alert firms to factors that can increase their vulnerability to geopolitical tensions.

Title: Cross-border effects of US FCPA enforcement: information and institutional spillovers in China through industry peers
Authors: Haijie Huang, Jeong-Bon Kim, Edward Lee, Junsheng Zhang
Abstract: We examine whether and how the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) drives intra-industry information spillovers that propagate cross-border institutional spillovers in China. Regulatory disclosures of FCPA enforcement actions against US firms can influence non-violating Chinese firms in the same industry through either (1) contagion risk arising from increased anti-corruption scrutiny in China or (2) competitive advantage due to reduced competition from US counterparts. Consistent with the contagion risk (competitive advantage) effect, we provide evidence over the 2011–2023 sample period that Securities and Exchange Commission disclosures of China-related (non-China-related) FCPA violations by US peer firms generate valuation discounts (premiums) among non-violating Chinese focal firms that are more likely to be suspected of corruption. Further analyses reveal subsequent decreases (increases) in profitability and suspected corruption spending among these Chinese firms. Our findings suggest that FCPA-related regulatory disclosures play an information subsidy role given the lack of transparency regarding corruption activities and serve as a form of institutional subsidy that promotes monitoring against such practices in weaker regulatory environments. While the pros and cons of the FCPA for US firms remain debatable, our study implies that international coordination and collaboration in anti-corruption enforcement should be strengthened to curb bribery in international business.

Title: Privacy trade-offs in international markets
Authors: Natalie Chisam, Jordan W. Moffett, Frank Germann, Robert W. Palmatier
Abstract: Abstract Even as data privacy regulations expand globally, their strategic implications for international business remain underexplored. Prior research mostly treats data privacy regulation as a compliance issue, overlooking how firms strategically manage cross-border variations and respond to stakeholder pressures. Drawing on institutional economics and stakeholder theory, this article conceptualizes two trade-offs generated by data privacy regulations: (1) a regulatory, cost–benefit trade-off between privacy compliance costs and customer privacy empowerment and (2) a firm performance, temporal trade-off in which early compliance costs undermine short-term outcomes, before longer-term, trust-based benefits emerge. An international event study of ten regulations across 24 countries affirms that data privacy regulations impose short-term financial setbacks but generate long-term gains. These effects vary across contexts: At regulation, industry, and firm levels, conditions in which internal pressures to minimize risk dominate (intense privacy regulation, strong data dependence, limited resources) intensify early losses. At national levels, environments dominated by external pressures for credible compliance (high formal and informal institutional effectiveness) offset short-term losses and magnify long-term benefits. For international business theory, this study reframes data privacy regulation as a strategic opportunity and highlights how internal versus external legitimacy pressures shape trade-offs that firms must balance to navigate cross-border compliance demands.

Title: Parallel internationalization during radical industry transformations: the case of Telecom Finland
Abstract: Abstract We examine how radical industry transformations shape firms’ internationalization, addressing the limited theorization of how industry-level dynamicsinfluence internationalization processes. Drawing on a historical case study of Telecom Finland’s internationalization during two radical transformations in the European telecommunications industry (1987–1998), we show how industry transformation simultaneously orients firms toward parallel internationalization and constrains its execution through systemic industry uncertainty, leading to two contributions. First, we offer an industry-driven explanation for why firms internationalize into multiple markets in parallel. Industry transformation enables parallel entries by creating simultaneous opportunities and actively orienting firms toward parallelism, as industry conditions shape what managers interpret as viable responses. Second, we expand understanding of uncertainty in internationalization processes by introducing the concept of systemic industry uncertainty, a form of transformation-driven uncertainty originating at the industry level, shared across actors, interdependent across markets, and irreducible within the relevant decision windows. Distinct from the market-specific uncertainty emphasized in internationalization process literature, systemic industry uncertainty impedes established uncertainty-reduction mechanisms—learning, network-based knowledge, and diversification—showing that uncertainty shapes internationalization in previously unrecognized ways. Our findings suggest that managers should closely follow industry-level developments, as these play a more central role in shaping internationalization than existing models assume.

Title: Revisiting the Uppsala model from a history-to-theory perspective: New lessons on network positioning from a global electric company
Authors: Alvaro Ferreira Silva, Emanuel Gomes, Ferran Vendrell-Herrero, David W. Lehman
Abstract: A firm cannot internationalize on its own. Rather, a network of multiple firms is critical. Accordingly, the Uppsala model has been reformulated in recent years to account for the role of networks in the firm internationalization process. Still unclear, however, is how a firm’s network position evolves—both within individual foreign market entries and across successive entries—under changing firm, industry, and macro conditions. This study utilizes the historical case method to address this gap. Specifically, it examines the birth, rise, and global dominance of Sofina, a Belgian electric company, as it entered various foreign markets from the turn of the 20th century until the start of the Second World War. Our analysis highlights network positioning as a dynamic process that unfolds both within and across market entries. Importantly, these processes are facilitated by ongoing firm commitments of financial, managerial, and physical resources, and are linked to different sources of organizational learning. They are also shaped by global events as well as firm- and industry-level factors. The explanatory model that emerges from this analysis suggests that firms may need to be more agile than previously acknowledged by continuously repositioning themselves within networks to successfully expand their global footprints.

Title: Indigenization as a distinct path of expropriation: French and US investments in Spain, 1870s–1959
Authors: Adoración Álvaro-Moya, Rafael Castro Balaguer, Caterina Moschieri
Abstract: This study examines why and how multinational corporations (MNCs) may see their local assets transferred to or absorbed by their host-country partners. Drawing on transaction cost economics, we argue that factors beyond the traditional ones proposed by international business research—e.g., entry mode, country risk, or elite ties—can help explain this indigenization of MNC subsidiaries. Using a comparative historical analysis of French and US MNCs operating in Spain from the 1870s to 1959 and an in-depth analysis of the French Banque de Paris et des Pay-Bas (Paribas) and US International Telephone & Telegraph (ITT), we examine why similar investment strategies and partnerships with the local elite led to divergent outcomes under increasing political instability and economic nationalism in Spain. French subsidiaries became more likely than their US counterparts to be indigenized by local partners, due to their operations in maturing sectors and the local partners’ growing ability to substitute foreign capabilities, shifting asset complementarities. Our findings advance the international business literature by conceptualizing indigenization as a distinct mechanism through which an MNC may see its assets expropriated by its local partners, often via strategic and discretionary transfer shaped by shifting complementarities, maturing industries, and persistent relational ties. Este estudio examina por qué y cómo las empresas multinacionales (EMN) pueden ver sus activos locales transferidos o absorbidos por sus socios en el país anfitrión. Basándonos en la economía de costos de transacción, argumentamos que factores más allá de los tradicionales propuestos por la investigación en negocios internacionales —por ejemplo, el modo de entrada, el riesgo país o los vínculos con las élites— pueden ayudar a explicar esta indigenización de las subsidiarias de las EMN. Utilizando un análisis histórico comparativo de las EMN francesas y estadounidenses que operaron en España desde la década de 1870 hasta 1959, y un análisis en profundidad del Banque de Paris et des Pay-Bas (Paribas) francés y de la International Telephone & Telegraph (ITT) estadounidense, examinamos por qué estrategias de inversión similares y alianzas con las élites locales llevaron a resultados divergentes bajo una creciente inestabilidad política y un nacionalismo económico en España. Las subsidiarias francesas se volvieron más propensas que sus contrapartes estadounidenses a ser indigenizadas por socios locales, debido a sus operaciones en sectores en maduración y a la creciente capacidad de los socios locales para sustituir las capacidades extranjeras, modificando las complementariedades de activos. Nuestros hallazgos avanzan en la literatura de negocios internacionales al conceptualizar la indigenización como un mecanismo distinto mediante el cual una EMN puede ver sus activos expropiados por sus socios locales, a menudo a través de transferencias estratégicas y discrecionales moldeadas por complementariedades cambiantes, industrias en maduración y vínculos relacionales persistentes Este estudo examina porque e como corporações multinacionais (MNCs) podem ver seus ativos locais transferidos ou absorvidos por seus parceiros no país anfitrião. Com base na economia de custos de transação, argumentamos que fatores além dos tradicionais propostos pela pesquisa em negócios internacionais — por exemplo, modo de entrada, risco-país ou conexões com elites — podem ajudar a explicar essa indigenização de subsidiárias de MNCs. Title: Reclaiming history in IB research: expanding interdisciplinary inquiry through historical contextualization
Authors: Stephanie Decker, Geoffrey Jones, Klaus E. Meyer, Rebecca Piekkari, Catherine Welch
Abstract: La historia no es meramente un prólogo para la investigación en Negocios Internacionales (NI); es un elemento constitutivo de cómo entendemos las empresas multinacionales, la entrada en mercados extranjeros, el cambio institucional y la creación de valor transfronterizo. A pesar del creciente reconocimiento de la colaboración interdisciplinaria, los académicos de Negocios Internacionales aún no tienen claro cómo integrar rigurosamente los métodos históricos y los conocimientos provenientes de la Historia Empresarial. En esta introducción al número especial, abordamos los impedimentos para una colaboración interdisciplinaria más estrecha entre las dos disciplinas. Identificamos tres puntos críticos de clarificación: la distancia temporal, las fuentes de archivos y la contextualización histórica. Proponemos diseños de investigación integradores que incorporen el análisis histórico directamente en la teorización de Negocios Internacionales. Dichos diseños de investigación permiten a los académicos de Negocios Internacionalesabordar preguntas causales, explorar efectos de legado y desarrollar teorías sensibles al tiempo y al contexto. La investigación de Negocios Internacionales contextualizada históricamente puede explicar por qué las teorías estandarizadas fallan en contextos específicos, revelar secuencias dependientes del camino que los análisis cuantitativos instantáneos no detectan y desarrollar teorías que consideren variaciones institucionales y temporales profundas. Establecemos criterios de evaluación para una investigación histórica rigurosa y creamos puentes entre la investigación en Negocios Internacionales y la Historia Empresarial. Al clarificar conceptos, proporcionar diseños de investigación y modelar mejores prácticas, este número especial amplía la capacidad explicativa de los Negocios Internacionales para los fenómenos arraigados en el tiempo y sensibles al contexto que definen los negocios internacionales. A história não é meramente um prólogo para a pesquisa em Negócios Internacionais (IB) — ela é um elemento constitutivo de como entendemos as empresas multinacionais, a entrada em mercados estrangeiros, a mudança institucional e a criação de valor transfronteiriça. Apesar do crescente reconhecimento da colaboração interdisciplinar, acadêmicos de IB ainda não têm clareza sobre como integrar rigorosamente métodos históricos e insights da História Empresarial. Nesta introdução à edição especial, abordamos os impedimentos à colaboração interdisciplinar mais próxima entre as duas disciplinas. Identificamos três pontos críticos de esclarecimento: distância temporal, fontes arquivísticas e contextualização histórica. Propomos designs de pesquisa integrativos que incorporam análise histórica diretamente na teorização de IB. Esses designs de pesquisa permitem que acadêmicos de IB abordem questões causais, explorem efeitos de legado e desenvolvam teorias sensíveis ao tempo e ao contexto. A pesquisa em IB contextualizada historicamente pode explicar por que teorias padronizadas falham em contextos específicos, revelar sequências dependentes do caminho que instantâneos quantitativos não capturam e desenvolver teorias que considerem variações institucionais e temporais profundas. Estabelecemos critérios de avaliação para pesquisas históricas rigorosas e criamos pontes entre os estudos de IB e de História Empresarial. Ao esclarecer conceitos, fornecer designs de pesquisa e modelar melhores práticas, esta edição especial expande a capacidade explicativa de IB para os fenômenos embutidos no tempo e sensíveis ao contexto que definem os negócios internacionais. 历史不仅仅是国际商业 (IB) 研究的序幕——它构成了我们理解跨国企业、外国市场进入、制度变迁以及跨境价值创造的一个核心构成要素。尽管跨学科合作日益受到认可, IB学者对于如何严谨地整合历史方法和商业史的洞见仍不清晰。在本期特刊的引言中, 我们探讨了这两个学科之间更紧密的跨学科合作所面临的障碍。我们指出了三个需要明确的关键点: 时间距离、档案来源以及历史情境化。我们提出了将历史分析直接嵌入IB理论化的整合性研究设计。 这样的研究设计使IB学者能够解决因果关系问题, 探索遗留效应, 并发展对时间和情境敏感的理论。经过历史情境化的IB研究可以解释为什么标准化理论在特定情境中失效, 揭示定量快照所忽略的路径依赖序列, 并发展能够解释深层制度与时间变迁的理论。 我们确立了评估严谨历史研究的标准, 并在IB和商业史学术研究之间架起桥梁。通过澄清

Title: High-investment human resource practices and firm performance in the context of national education systems and labor markets: A cross-national meta-analysis
Authors: Joo Hun Han, Saehee Kang, David G. Allen, Yan Pan
Abstract: Abstract Organizations—especially multinational corporations (MNCs)—do not always realize comparable performance gains from investing in people across national borders. Prior research has attempted to explain such variation in the effects of high-investment human resource practices (HIHRPs) by emphasizing their fit with national cultural values, yet empirical support for this cultural fit perspective has been limited. To address this gap, we focus on national institutional factors that more directly shape how HIHRPs influence performance. Drawing on human capital resources (HCR) theory and institutional perspectives in International Business (IB), we identify two institutional conditions—national education quality and labor market flexibility—that moderate HIHRP effectiveness. We theorize that high-quality education systems enhance the HIHRPs–performance relationship by supplying workers with strong general human capital and that this effect is amplified in flexible labor markets where employees are motivated to contribute. A meta-analysis of 1,285 effect sizes from 170,938 organizations across 29 countries offers nuanced evidence: HIHRPs were more effective when national education quality and labor market flexibility were both high or both low than when they were mismatched. These findings advance comparative and strategic HRM research and guide organizations about how comprehensively or selectively to invest in managing people in what institutional contexts.

Title: Guilty as charged? Reassessing the problem of single-country samples in cultural distance studies
Abstract: Abstract Concerns have been raised about the use of single host- or home-country samples in analyzing the effects of cultural distance (CD). That is, the estimated effects of CD may be confounded with those of the underlying cultural dimensions or other contextual factors correlated with CD. This study reassesses the risk of confounding when using single-country samples through simulation analyses conducted under various conditions, including different sample sizes and structures, within- and between-country variances, and analysis methods. The results indicate that when other cultural or contextual variables related to the outcome are also included and multilevel modeling is applied, the risk of confounding is not significant across diverse settings. The problem of confounding becomes significant only when using ordinary least squares, which does not take into account the potential nonindependence of observations in hierarchical data. However, in multilevel analyses using single-country samples, statistical power may become insufficient when controlling for cultural variables correlated with CD, particularly when the effect size of CD is small. To address this issue, we present a statistical technique that researchers can use to identify potential confounders and provide guidelines on the sample size required to maintain adequate power.

Title: CEO-to-employee pay ratios, societal-level income inequality, and citizens’ subjective well-being
Authors: Kaifeng Jiang, Yingya Jia, Anne S. Tsui, Jia Yu
Abstract: A desigualdade de renda é um fenômeno mundial que preocupa cada vez mais acadêmicos, formuladores de políticas, líderes empresariais e cidadãos comuns. Com base na pesquisa que enfatiza o papel de empresas na formação dos resultados sociais, este estudo investiga como estruturas salariais organizacionais — especificamente a razão entre a remuneração do diretor executivo (CEO) e a de funcionários — estão relacionadas à desigualdade de renda em nível social e ao bem-estar subjetivo dos cidadãos. Utilizando uma base de dados em painel de 15 anos de 53 países, descobrimos que maiores razões entre a remuneração do CEO e a de funcionários estão significativamente associadas a aumentos na desigualdade de renda em nível social no ano seguinte. Com base na teoria da justiça social, também mostramos que razões entre a remuneração do CEO e a de funcionários estão negativamente relacionadas ao bem-estar subjetivo dos cidadãos no ano posterior, sendo maior do que os efeitos da desigualdade de renda em nível social e de outras condições nacionais. Descobrimos ainda que essa associação negativa é mais acentuada em países com um estado de bem-estar social mais elevado. Em conjunto, essas descobertas avançam a pesquisa sobre desigualdade, bem-estar e negócios internacionais ao mostrar como estruturas de remuneração em nível empresarial moldam resultados sociais mais amplos. Essas descobertas também oferecem implicações práticas para líderes corporativos e formuladores de políticas que buscam compreender como a estrutura de remuneração corporativa vai além das organizações para afetar a desigualdade econômica na sociedade e o bem-estar dos cidadãos. La desigualdad de ingresos es un fenómeno mundial que preocupa cada vez más a académicos, formuladores de políticas, líderes empresariales y ciudadanos comunes. Basándose en investigaciones que destacan el papel de las empresas en la configuración de los resultados sociales, este estudio investiga cómo las estructuras salariales organizacionales (específicamente los ratios salariales entre el director ejecutivo (CEO) y los empleados) se relacionan con la desigualdad de ingresos a nivel social y el bienestar subjetivo de los ciudadanos. Utilizando datos de panel de 15 años que abarcan 53 países, encontramos que ratios salariales más altos entre el CEO y los empleados están significativamente asociados con aumentos en la desigualdad de ingresos a nivel social al año siguiente. Basándonos en la teoría de la justicia social, también mostramos que los ratios salariales entre el CEO y los empleados están negativamente relacionados con el bienestar subjetivo de los ciudadanos un año después, más allá de los efectos de la desigualdad de ingresos a nivel social y otras condiciones nacionales. Además, descubrimos que esta asociación negativa es más pronunciada en países con un estado de bienestar más sólido. En conjunto, estos hallazgos avanzan en la investigación sobre desigualdad, bienestar y negocios internacionales al mostrar cómo las estructuras de compensación a nivel empresarial moldean los resultados sociales más amplios. Estos hallazgos también ofrecen implicaciones accionables para los líderes corporativos y los formuladores de políticas que buscan comprender cómo la estructura salarial corporativa trasciende las organizaciones para afectar la desigualdad económica en la sociedad y el bienestar de los ciudadanos. 收入不平等是一个全球性现象, 它越来越受到学者、政策制定者、商业领袖和普通公民的关注。本研究以强调企业在塑造社会成果中的作用的研究为基础, 调查了组织薪酬结构——特别是首席执行官 (CEO) 与员工薪酬比率——如何与社会层面收入不平等和公民主观幸福感相关联。通过分析一个涵盖53个国家、为期15年的面板数据集, 我们发现较高的CEO与员工薪酬比率与下一年度社会层面收入不平等的加剧显著相关。借鉴社会正义理论, 我们的分析还表明, 在控制了社会层面收入不平等和其他影响因素之后，CEO与员工薪酬比率与一年后公民的主观幸福感仍呈显著负相关。我们进一步发现, 在政府福利支出和收入再分配程度较高的国家中，这种负相关关系更加显著。这些发现通过展示企业层面的薪酬结构如何产生更为广泛的社会影响, 推动了关于不平等、幸福感和国际商业的研究。这些发现还为企业领导者和政策制定者理解企业薪酬结构如何延伸到组织之外、进而影响社会经济不平等和公民幸福感，提供了具有实践意义的启示。 Income inequality is a worldwide phenomenon that increasingly concerns scholars, policy-makers, business leaders, and ordinary citizens. Title: Once sued, twice shy: international litigation, trust radius, and international expansion
Authors: Xuchang Chen, Han Li, Jingjing Yao
Abstract: O mundo está testemunhando um aumento nos conflitos interorganizacionais além-fronteiras, mas o impacto desses conflitos na expansão internacional de empresas permanece amplamente inexplorado. Com base na teoria do contato intergrupal, teorizamos que o envolvimento em conflitos com uma empresa estrangeira constitui uma forma de contato intergrupal negativo, que pode se espalhar para atitudes desfavoráveis mais amplas — não apenas em relação à entidade estrangeira envolvida, mas também ao mercado estrangeiro de forma mais ampla. Especificamente, prevemos que o envolvimento em litígios internacionais desencoraja uma empresa de empreender a expansão internacional. Além disso, esse efeito negativo de transbordamento pode ser mitigado pelo raio de confiança — a amplitude do círculo de cooperação dentro de uma sociedade. Empresas inseridas em regiões com um raio de confiança mais amplo e, portanto, habituadas a interagir com grupos diversos, são menos afetadas por litígios internacionais. Resultados de uma amostra de empresas chinesas de capital aberto apoiam nossas hipóteses. Ao testar e expandir a teoria do contato intergrupal na pesquisa em negócios internacionais, estabelecemos uma conexão teórica entre conflito interorganizacional e expansão internacional, e também destacamos o raio de confiança como um fator-chave que contribui para dinâmicas de contato intergrupal das empresas. El mundo está presenciando un aumento en los conflictos interorganizacionales transfronterizos, pero su impacto en la expansión internacional de las empresas permanece en gran medida inexplorado. Basándonos en la teoría del contacto intergrupal, teorizamos que la participación en un conflicto con una empresa extranjera constituye una forma de contacto intergrupal negativo, lo cual puede derivar en actitudes desfavorables más amplias, no solo hacia la entidad extranjera específica involucrada, sino también hacia el mercado extranjero en general. Específicamente, predecimos que la participación en litigios internacionales desalienta a una empresa de emprender una expansión internacional. Además, este efecto de derrame negativo puede ser mitigado por el radio de confianza, es decir, la amplitud del círculo de cooperación dentro de una sociedad. Las empresas ubicadas en regiones con un radio de confianza más amplio, y por lo tanto acostumbradas a interactuar con grupos diversos, se ven menos afectadas por los litigios internacionales. Los resultados de una muestra de empresas chinas que cotizan en bolsa respaldan nuestras hipótesis. Al probar y extender la teoría del contacto intergrupal en la investigación de negocios internacionales, establecemos un vínculo teórico entre el conflicto interorganizacional y la expansión internacional, y también destacamos el radio de confianza como un factor clave que contribuye a las dinámicas de contacto intergrupal de las empresas. The article explores how international litigation affects firms' willingness to expand globally, particularly through foreign direct investment (FDI). As businesses increasingly enter global markets, they face conflicts due to cultural and regulatory differences. Recent geopolitical tensions have exacerbated these issues, leading to a rise in international business disputes. The study investigates whether involvement in litigation with foreign entities discourages firms from international expansion and how this negative impact might be mitigated. The key finding is that international litigation can indeed discourage firms from expanding internationally, but this effect can be mitigated by a wider "trust radius"—the extent to which a society's cooperative norms include both ingroup and outgroup members. This article uses data from 3671 publicly listed Chinese firms from 2001 to 2018 to examine the impact of international litigation on FDI. Title: Banking system stability: a global analysis of cybercrime laws
Authors: Douglas Cumming, My Nguyen, Anh Viet Pham, Ama Samarasinghe
Abstract: Abstract We examine the role of cybercrime legislation globally in shaping the stability of the banking system. We compile a novel dataset covering the enactment of cybercrime legislation in 132 developed and developing countries to test this research question empirically. We find that the enactment of cybercrime laws enhances the stability of the banking sector. This key finding holds across a comprehensive suite of robustness tests, including alternative measures of bank stability and model specifications. We document significant cross-sectional heterogeneity, with the effect being more pronounced in countries with heavier penalties for illegal cyber activities and legal frameworks that hold banks accountable for their cybersecurity practices. Moreover, the positive impact is stronger in jurisdictions with greater international legal cooperation and effective enforcement mechanisms. We further investigate two channels (i.e., funding liquidity and operational risk) through which cybercrime laws may influence bank stability. Our results indicate that these laws can significantly bolster bank stability by enhancing funding liquidity and mitigating operational risk. Overall, our study provides evidence of the crucial role of cybercrime legislation in fostering a secure and resilient banking environment. It offers new insights into how these laws contribute to bank stability on both individual and systemic levels.

Title: Bottom-up innovation under uncertainty: the role of face concerns in shaping overt and covert innovation across cultures
Authors: Jinzhao Qu, Svetlana N. Khapova, Yipeng Tang
Abstract: A maior parte das pesquisas sobre inovação de baixo para cima enfatiza que os funcionários inovam ao adotar a incerteza, uma visão enraizada em culturas anglo-saxônicas que valorizam a exposição a riscos. No entanto, países influenciados por tradições confucionistas, que priorizam a harmonia e a evasão de conflitos, também alcançam resultados fortes em inovação, apresentando um paradoxo cultural. Abordamos esse paradoxo introduzindo a preocupação com a "imagem", o desejo de manter ou melhorar a imagem social, como um mecanismo culturalmente específico que molda o comportamento inovador. Conceituamos a incerteza na inovação como sendo de duas naturezas: envolvendo incerteza na tarefa e incerteza social. A presença de colegas inovadores reduz a incerteza na tarefa e incentiva a inovação, mas também aumenta a incerteza social, ativando preocupações com a " imagem " culturalmente distintas. Em contextos anglo-saxônicos, a preocupação com a "imagem" focada na promoção leva funcionários com baixa aversão à incerteza a se engajarem em inovação aberta e explícita. Em contraste, em contextos confucionistas, a preocupação com a "imagem" focada na prevenção leva funcionários com alta aversão à incerteza a buscarem inovação de forma velada. Testamos essas hipóteses por meio de dois estudos: um experimento baseado em cenários e uma pesquisa multinacional conduzida nos Estados Unidos, no Reino Unido, no Japão e na China. Os resultados apoiam nossas previsões, revelando que orientações culturais moldam como os funcionários lidam com a incerteza na inovação. Esta pesquisa avança na compreensão da inovação de baixo para cima ao destacar os mecanismos culturalmente contingentes que promovem formas distintas de comportamento inovador. La plupart des recherches sur l'innovation ascendante soulignent que les employés innovent en embrassant l'incertitude, une vision enracinée dans les cultures anglo-saxonnes qui valorisent la prise de risque. Cependant, les pays influencés par les traditions confucéennes, qui privilégient l'harmonie et l'évitement des conflits, obtiennent également des résultats solides en matière d'innovation, ce qui présente un paradoxe culturel. Nous abordons ce paradoxe en introduisant la notion de préoccupations liées à la face, c'est-à-dire le désir de maintenir ou d'améliorer son image sociale, comme un mécanisme culturellement spécifique influençant le comportement en matière d’innovation. Nous conceptualisons l'incertitude liée à l'innovation comme étant double, impliquant une incertitude liée aux tâches et une incertitude sociale. La présence de collègues innovants réduit l'incertitude liée aux tâches et encourage l'innovation, mais augmente également l'incertitude sociale, activant ainsi des préoccupations liées à la face culturellement distinctes. Dans les contextes anglo-saxons, une préoccupation liée à la face axée sur la promotion pousse les employés ayant une faible aversion pour l'incertitude à s'engager dans une innovation ouverte. En revanche, dans les contextes confucéens, une préoccupation liée à la face axée sur la prévention conduit les employés ayant une forte aversion pour l'incertitude à poursuivre une innovation discrète. Nous testons ces hypothèses à travers deux études : une expérience basée sur des scénarios et une enquête multi-pays menée aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni, au Japon et en Chine. Les résultats confirment nos prédictions, révélant que les orientations culturelles façonnent la manière dont les employés naviguent dans l'incertitude liée à l'innovation. Cette recherche fait progresser la compréhension de l'innovation ascendante en mettant en lumière les mécanismes culturellement contingents qui favorisent des formes distinctes de comportement innovant.c La mayoría de las investigaciones sobre la innovación ascendente enfatizan que los empleados innovan al aceptar la incertidumbre, una perspectiva arraigada en las culturas anglosajonas que valoran la asunción de riesgos. Title: Digital dampening and internationalization of digital firms
Authors: Siddharth Natarajan, Qingwei Li, Seung Ho Park
Abstract: To examine heterogeneity in the internationalization of digital firms, we introduce the concept of “digital dampening”, which refers to the extent to which non-digital elements are integrated into a digital firm. We argue that digital dampening inhibits internationalization. We develop testable hypotheses about the international multihoming of smartphone apps from China and analyze rich data on 33,878 smartphone apps from 25,233 Chinese vendors on the Tencent app market. Our methodology leverages generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in conjunction with latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) to investigate how the digital dampening of Tencent apps influences their presence on Google Play, a foreign app market. The findings indicate that the digital dampening of Tencent apps is negatively associated with their presence on Google Play, particularly for apps that face weaker downloads compared to their rivals. Supplementary analyses shed light on post-internationalization metrics on Google Play and vendor-level extensive and intensive margins of internationalization. Further tests rule out plausible alternative explanations and verify sensitivity for GenAI usage. Overall, the study presents an alternative to the prevailing view of born-digital firms as inherently global, emphasizing that non-digital complementarities in the business model can hinder internationalization, particularly in those firms facing a weak domestic competitive position. Para examinar a heterogeneidade na internacionalização de empresas digitais, introduzimos o conceito de “amortecimento digital”, que se refere ao grau em que elementos não digitais são integrados a uma empresa digital. Argumentamos que o amortecimento digital inibe a internacionalização. Desenvolvemos hipóteses testáveis sobre o multihoming internacional de aplicativos de smartphone da China e analisamos dados abrangentes de 33.878 aplicativos de smartphone de 25.233 fornecedores chineses no mercado de aplicativos da Tencent. Nossa metodologia utiliza inteligência artificial generativa (GenAI) em conjunto com a Alocação Latente de Dirichlet (LDA) para investigar como o amortecimento digital dos aplicativos da Tencent influencia sua presença no Google Play, um mercado de aplicativos estrangeiro. Os resultados indicam que o amortecimento digital dos aplicativos da Tencent está negativamente associado à sua presença no Google Play, particularmente para aplicativos que enfrentam downloads mais anêmicos em comparação com seus concorrentes. Análises suplementares esclarecem métricas pós-internacionalização no Google Play e margens extensivas e intensivas de internacionalização no nível de fornecedores. Testes adicionais descartam explicações alternativas plausíveis e verificam a sensibilidade do uso de GenAI. De forma geral, o estudo apresenta uma alternativa à visão predominante de empresas nascidas digitais como inerentemente globais, enfatizando que complementaridades não digitais no modelo de negócios podem dificultar a internacionalização, especialmente em empresas que enfrentam uma posição competitiva doméstica fraca. 为了研究数字企业国际化过程中的异质性， 我们引入了“数字阻尼”的概念， 它指的是非数字元素整合于数字企业的程度。我们认为， 数字阻尼抑制了国际化。我们针对中国智能手机应用的国际多属（international multihoming）提出了可检验的假设， 并分析了来自腾讯应用市场的25,233家中国供应商的33,878款智能手机应用的丰富数据。我们的研究方法利用生成式人工智能（GenAI）与潜在狄利克雷分布（LDA）的结合， 调查了腾讯应用的数字阻尼如何影响其在海外应用市场Google Play上的存在。研究结果表明， 腾讯应用的数字阻尼与其在Google Play上的存在呈负相关关系， 尤其是对于那些与竞争对手相比下载量较弱的应用而言。补充分析揭示了这些应用在Google Play上的后国际化指标， 以及供应商层面国际化的外延边际和内涵边际。进一步的测试排除了其它合理的替代解释， 并验证了GenAI 使用的敏感性。总体而言， 本研究为当前的将“天生数字化企业”视为固有全球化的主流观点提供了一个替代视角， 强调了商业模式中的非数字互补性可能会阻碍国际化， 特别是对于那些国内竞争地位较弱的企业。 Pour examiner l'hétérogénéité dans l'internationalisation des entreprises numériques, nous introduisons le concept d’atténuation numérique (Digital Dampening), qui fait référence au degré auquel des éléments non numériques sont intégrés dans une entreprise numérique. Title: Global meets local: community political ideology and Chinese cross-border M&As in the U.S.
Authors: Yinuo Tang, Juan Bu, Danqing Wang, Weilei Shi
Abstract: The article explores how political ideology within local communities affects the success of cross-border mergers and acquisitions (M&As) between rival countries, specifically focusing on Chinese firms acquiring U.S. companies. The study addresses a gap in understanding how macro-level political ideologies, such as community conservatism, influence international business (IB) activities. The key finding is that conservative communities in the U.S. are more likely to resist M&As from Chinese firms due to perceived threats and uncertainties, reducing the likelihood of deal completion. This article uses data from 267 M&A deals by Chinese public firms in the U.S. from 2002 to 2021. The researchers analyzed how community political ideology, measured by the percentage of votes for Republican candidates in presidential elections, impacts the completion of these deals. They argue that conservative communities perceive higher threats and uncertainties from foreign acquisitions, especially from rival countries like China. The study also considers factors like whether the M&A targets sensitive industries (critical to national security) and the economic distress of the target community. These factors can amplify the perceived threats and uncertainties, further decreasing the likelihood of deal completion. The results show that Chinese M&As in conservative U.S. communities are less likely to be completed. This effect is stronger when the deals involve sensitive industries or when the target communities face economic distress. The study concludes that community political ideology is a significant factor in the success of cross-border M&As, highlighting the need for multinational enterprises (MNEs) to consider local political climates when planning investments. The research advances understanding of how subnational political factors influence IB and suggests that MNEs should engage with local stakeholders to mitigate resistance. Future implications include exploring other political ideologies and their effects on international business strategies. La intensificación de la rivalidad entre las principales economías globales resalta la necesidad de comprender mejor la naturaleza politizada de los negocios internacionales. Este estudio introduce un nuevo factor político: la ideología política comunitaria (es decir, la ideología política dominante a lo largo del espectro liberalismo-conservadurismo entre los miembros de una comunidad) y examina su influencia en las fusiones y adquisiciones transfronterizas (F&A transfronterizas) entre países considerados rivales económicos y políticos. Basándonos en la literatura sobre ideología política y F&A transfronterizas, argumentamos que las comunidades conservadoras tienden a percibir mayores amenazas e incertidumbre derivadas de las F&A transfronterizas provenientes de países rivales y, por lo tanto, oponen mayor resistencia a estas operaciones. Utilizando las F&A transfronterizas chinas en Estados Unidos como contexto de investigación, predecimos que estas F&A tienen menos probabilidades de concretarse en comunidades estadounidenses con una mayor proporción de residentes conservadores. Además, el efecto negativo del conservadurismo comunitario sobre la concreción de operaciones de F&A chinas en Estados Unidos se intensifica aún más cuando las empresas objetivo pertenecen a industrias sensibles o cuando las comunidades objetivo atraviesan mayores dificultades económicas. Title: Multinationals’ solutions to Grand Challenges
Authors: Alvaro Cuervo-Cazurra, Grazia D. Santangelo, Gerard George, Laszlo Tihanyi, Jonathan Doh, Lemma W. Senbet, Xufei Ma
Abstract: Grand Challenges are complex problems that transcend national borders and affect future generations and, as a result, have traditionally been viewed as the responsibility of governments. Building on economic theories of market imperfections, we introduce a three-pronged framework to explain how multinationals contribute solutions to Grand Challenges. First, we clarify multinationals’ solutions by classifying them by their sustainability dimensions and associated market imperfections: solutions to environmental Grand Challenges arising from negative externalities and the overexploitation of common goods; solutions to social Grand Challenges resulting from unrealized positive externalities and underinvestment in public goods; and solutions to governance Grand Challenges stemming from information imperfections and abuses of market power. Second, we contextualize the global implementation of these solutions within the two drivers of globalization (technological and institutional changes) and explain their supporting and constraining effects: technological advances enable cross-border development and coordination, but technological inertia and lock-in produce suboptimal outcomes; pro-market reforms facilitate cross-border diffusion, but pro-market reversals limit global knowledge transfer. Third, we explain how intersectoral collaboration and financing are supplementary drivers enabling the scaling of multinationals’ solutions across countries. Overall, our framework resolves the paradox that multinationals can help solve, rather than exploit, market failures. Grandes Desafios são problemas complexos que transcendem fronteiras nacionais e afetam as gerações futuras e, como resultado, têm sido tradicionalmente vistos como responsabilidade dos governos. Com base em teorias econômicas sobre imperfeições de mercado, introduzimos uma estrutura de três pilares para explicar como as multinacionais contribuem com soluções para Grandes Desafios. Primeiramente, esclarecemos soluções de multinacionais classificando-as de acordo com suas dimensões de sustentabilidade e associadas imperfeições de mercado: soluções para Grandes Desafios ambientais decorrentes de externalidades negativas e da superexploração de bens comuns; soluções para Grandes Desafios sociais decorrentes de externalidades positivas não realizadas e de subinvestimento em bens públicos; e soluções para Grandes Desafios de governança originados de imperfeições de informação e abusos de poder de mercado. Em segundo lugar, contextualizamos a implementação global dessas soluções no âmbito de dois impulsionadores da globalização (mudanças tecnológicas e institucionais) e explicamos seus efeitos de apoio e restrição: avanços tecnológicos permitem o desenvolvimento e a coordenação transfronteiriça, mas a inércia tecnológica e o aprisionamento tecnológico produzem resultados subótimos; reformas pró-mercado facilitam a difusão transfronteiriça, mas retrocessos pró-mercado limitam a transferência global de conhecimento. Em terceiro lugar, explicamos como a colaboração intersetorial e o financiamento são impulsionadores suplementares que possibilitam a ampliação das soluções de multinacionais entre os países. De forma geral, nosso modelo soluciona o paradoxo de que multinacionais podem ajudar a resolver, em vez de explorar, as falhas de mercado. 重大挑战是超越国界并影响后代的复杂问题， 因此传统上被视为政府的责任。基于市场缺陷的经济理论， 我们提出了一个三管齐下的框架， 以解释跨国公司如何为重大挑战贡献解决方案。首先， 我们通过可持续性维度和相关的市场缺陷对跨国公司的解决方案进行分类， 从而明确其解决方案：针对源于负外部性和公共资源过度开发的环境重大挑战的解决方案；针对源于未实现的正外部性和对公共产品投资不足的社会重大挑战的解决方案；以及针对源于信息不对称和市场力量滥用的治理重大挑战的解决方案。其次， 我们将这些解决方案的全球实施置于全球化的两大驱动因素（技术变革和制度变革）之中， 并解释其支持和限制作用：技术进步使跨境开发和协调成为可能， 但技术惯性与锁定效应会产生次优结果；亲市场改革促进了跨国扩散， 但亲市场逆转限制了全球知识转移。第三， 我们解释了跨部门合作和融资如何作为补充驱动因素推动跨国公司解决方案在各国的规模化。总体而言， 我们的框架解决了一个悖论， 即跨国公司能帮助解决市场失灵， 而非利用市场失灵。 Les Grands Défis sont des problèmes complexes qui transcendent les frontières nationales et affectent les générations futures. Title: Trapped in the MNE matrix: liminal identity at the local–corporate–global nexus
Authors: Kieran M. Conroy, David G. Collings
Abstract: Abstract Managers’ identities in large matrixed MNE structures are complex and pliable. While research has examined the identities of individual actors located in headquarters (HQ) or local subsidiaries, the unique identity challenges faced by those operating outside these conventional units are less predictable. Our study explores how managers experience and manage a ‘liminal identity’—feeling ‘betwixt and between’ multiple identity positions. Focusing on US MNEs in the life sciences sector, we interviewed managers who assumed global responsibilities from corporate HQ while remaining situated in their local (Irish) subsidiary. We find that operating between corporate HQ, a global network, and the local subsidiary forged a liminal identity. Straddling this local–corporate–global nexus was a profoundly ambiguous, precarious, and destabilizing experience. Yet, individuals also sought to leverage their liminal identity by adopting multiple identities, depending on the audience. This involved ‘switching’ between renouncing a local identity, assimilating a corporate identity and co-constructing a global identity. However, this produced an intense identity struggle, eroding a clear sense of self and belonging. Our study cautions firms to be attentive when supporting managers in these ‘in-between’ spaces to avoid the trap of ‘identity limbo’, where individuals risk becoming disconnected and isolated.

Title: Reflections on the 2025 JIBS Decade Award: “Institutions and social entrepreneurship: The role of institutional voids, institutional support, and institutional configurations”
Digital transformation and the offshore outsourcing behavior of manufacturing MNEs
Authors: Jeoung Yul Lee, Lin Cui, Chinmay Pattnaik, Byungchul Choi
Abstract: Este estudo analisa o impacto da transformação digital na intensidade de terceirização offshore de empresas multinacionais (MNEs) do setor de manufatura. Distinguimos duas categorias independentes de transformação digital: centrada em informação (IDT) e centrada em manufatura (MDT). Aplicando a teoria de custos de transação (TCE), argumentamos que a IDT reduz a intensidade da terceirização offshore, enquanto a MDT a aumenta. Esses efeitos têm origem em suas respectivas influências na especificidade de ativos transacionais essenciais de uma MNE que agregam valor, da frequência e variabilidade de sua demanda por insumos complementares e na incerteza nas transações de mercado. Além disso, identificamos fatores internos e externos que fornecem salvaguardas regulatórias e relacionais para transações de mercado, dessa forma moderando esses efeitos. Testamos empiricamente nossas hipóteses utilizando 3.271 observações empresa-ano de 492 MNEs coreanas do setor de manufatura entre 2011 e 2021. Nossos resultados oferecem forte suporte a nossas hipóteses, destacando a relevância da TCE para compreender a governança da cadeia de suprimentos global de MNEs no contexto da transformação digital. This article explores how digital transformation affects the governance choices of multinational enterprises (MNEs) in global value chains (GVCs). Specifically, it examines how digital technologies influence whether MNEs choose offshore outsourcing or captive offshoring. The study identifies two types of digital transformation: information-centric digital transformation (IDT) and manufacturing-centric digital transformation (MDT). IDT focuses on creating new value through data analytics and innovation, while MDT aims to optimize production processes through technologies like robotics and the Internet of Things. The study investigates how these transformations impact MNEs’ decisions to outsource or insource and the role of external factors like intellectual property protection and local managerial expertise. This article uses transaction cost economics (TCE) to analyze how IDT and MDT affect MNEs’ offshore outsourcing intensity. TCE is a theory that explains how firms choose between making products in-house or buying them from external suppliers based on costs. The study examines Korean manufacturing MNEs from 2011 to 2021, analyzing data from 492 firms. It uses content analysis of annual reports to measure the extent of IDT and MDT. The study also considers how intellectual property protection and local managerial expertise in offshore locations influence these decisions. The research finds that IDT tends to decrease offshore outsourcing because it creates firm-specific data that is best kept within the company. In contrast, MDT encourages outsourcing by enabling modular and automated production processes that reduce transaction costs. The study concludes that digital transformation does not uniformly impact MNE governance in GVCs. IDT and MDT have distinct effects on outsourcing decisions, influenced by external factors like intellectual property protection and local managerial expertise. The findings suggest that MNEs should strategically align their digital transformation efforts with their governance choices and consider the regulatory and managerial context of their offshore locations. Future research could explore these dynamics in different industries and regions to provide a more comprehensive understanding of digital transformation’s impact on international business strategies. Title: International involvement of managed ecosystems: a quasi-experiment of foreign user traffic to e-commerce platforms amid geopolitical conflicts
Authors: Rui Yang, Xinran Wang, Rongjian Yu, Crystal Zhan
Abstract: The rapid growth of digitalization has made e-commerce a key player in global trade. E-commerce connects buyers and sellers online, eliminating the need for physical stores. In 2023, e-commerce sales hit $5.82 trillion, making up nearly 20% of retail sales worldwide. Cross-border e-commerce is expanding at 17% annually, with a projected value of $2.25 trillion by 2026. Despite its importance, little research exists on how e-commerce platforms internationalize digitally. A recent study introduces "managed ecosystems," where platforms expand globally by leveraging other participants in their ecosystem, unlike traditional models that rely on physical presence. This study focuses on how these ecosystems attract international user traffic, especially through search engines like Google, which drive a significant portion of e-commerce visits. This article examines how e-commerce platforms attract foreign user traffic during disruptions, using the Russia–Ukraine conflict as a case study. The conflict serves as a quasi-experiment to analyze changes in user traffic to e-commerce platforms in neighboring countries compared to non-neighboring ones. The study uses a difference-in-differences (DiD) design to track these changes. It finds that platforms in neighboring countries saw increased foreign traffic when they could supply products around the conflict zone. The study also explores how platforms can actively shape their visibility on search engines through keyword strategies. Two strategies are identified: niche focus, which targets specific keywords for unique queries, and mass appeal, which targets popular keywords for broader reach. Both strategies enhanced the impact of the conflict on cross-border traffic. The study concludes that managed ecosystems play a crucial role in digital internationalization by focusing on user acquisition through search engines. It highlights the importance of search engines in connecting global buyers and sellers, facilitating international involvement of e-commerce platforms. The research also shows that geopolitical conflicts can create opportunities for platforms to expand their reach by adjusting their search engine strategies. Future implications include the potential for platforms to further optimize their search visibility and explore other digital channels for international expansion. Title: Real option portfolios and the theory of the multinational enterprise: understanding modes of international involvement in the digital economy
Abstract: Abstract The recent growth of the digital economy and technological advances has created new patterns of FDI and international involvement. We contribute to the debate on nontraditional (NT) entry modes in a changing digital world—virtual presence, digital platforms, and innovation outposts. We provide fresh insights into real option theory (ROT) and MNE theory, explaining new forms of international involvement within a dynamic ROT portfolio perspective. We discuss uncertainty and correlation among market conditions, knowledge redundancy, how NT modes entail MNE growth and switching options, and how they contribute to the MNE option portfolio. We discuss information options and other real options embedded in NT modes, and the factors influencing their values. Our article has practical relevance as many MNEs do not incorporate real options into their decision-making processes. We encourage managers to understand that (1) uncertainty influences options beneficially, (2) NT modes create real options, and (3) these NT options create flexibility. Our ROT ‘portfolio’ perspective shows how uncertainty, market correlation, and knowledge diversity influence a real option’s contribution to MNE option portfolios, though they are context-specific. Finally, we compare how ROT insights complement those from existing MNE theories.

Title: Digital institutions and virtual involvement of born-digital firms
Authors: Yinuo Tang, Yan Shen, Juan Bu, Dongfa Feng
Abstract: Empresas criadas no ambiente digital buscam cada vez mais envolvimento virtual, uma estratégia de entrada no mercado digital que prioriza a coleta iterativa de dados e a adaptação algorítmica em vez da expansão física. Medimos o envolvimento virtual pelo número de anúncios digitais únicos e o definimos como a intensidade da experimentação digital de uma empresa para coletar dados de usuários, treinar algoritmos e possibilitar aprendizado contínuo por meio de um ciclo de feedback recursivo. Utilizando um conjunto de dados inédito que abrange 194 empresas nascidas no ambiente digital nos EUA e na China, em 33 países, entre 2016 e 2022, nossa análise empírica revela que uma regulamentação rigorosa de privacidade digital no país anfitrião reduz significativamente o envolvimento virtual. Essa influência negativa é atenuada em maiores mercados digitais, para empresas de países de origem com regimes regulatórios digitais robustos e quando as empresas recebem sentimentos públicos positivos. Esses resultados ampliam a teoria institucional e a pesquisa não tradicional sobre modos de entrada ao introduzir o envolvimento virtual como uma nova dimensão da estratégia internacional sob restrições regulatórias. Para formuladores de políticas e gestores, nosso estudo oferece orientações práticas: regras rigorosas de privacidade protegem o bem-estar de usuários, mas condições de mercado favoráveis e experiência regulatória são cruciais para sustentar a inovação orientada por dados. Formuladores de políticas devem equilibrar a proteção dos usuários com o dinamismo do mercado, enquanto empresas devem aproveitar mercados grandes e sentimentos positivos para manter seu envolvimento virtual. Born-digital firms increasingly pursue virtual involvement, a digital market-entry strategy that prioritizes iterative data collection and algorithmic adaptation over physical expansion. We measure virtual involvement by the number of unique digital advertisements and define it as the intensity of a firm’s digital experimentation to collect user data, train algorithms, and enable continuous learning through a recursive feedback loop. Using a novel panel dataset covering 194 US and Chinese born-digital firms across 33 countries from 2016 to 2022, our empirical analysis finds that stringent host-country digital privacy regulation significantly reduces virtual involvement. This negative influence is weakened in larger digital markets, for firms from home countries with robust digital regulatory regimes, and when firms receive positive public sentiment. These results extend institutional theory and non-traditional entry mode research by introducing virtual involvement as a new dimension of international strategy under regulatory constraints. For policymakers and managers, our study offers actionable guidance: strict privacy rules protect user welfare, but supportive market conditions and regulatory experience are critical to sustaining data-driven innovation.
